# Implement task

Entry point for `/implement-task`. This skill routes to the orchestrator; it does
not restate the workflow. The orchestrator contract is authoritative, and it is the
only place the sequence is written down.

1. Resolve the active SharedVSCode worktree and read
   `.ai/agents/implement-task.agent.md` there. That file defines the arguments
   (`Task`, `Continue`, `Board`, `DryRun`), the numbered sequence, the hard stops,
   and the list of things the orchestrator never does. Follow it exactly; if this
   skill and that contract ever disagree, the contract wins.

2. Run the sequence in the **current session** rather than dispatching the
   orchestrator as a subagent. The approval gate in step 3 of the contract must
   reach a human, and a nested subagent has no reliable channel to one. Adopt the
   orchestrator role here; dispatch only the workers and support agents it names.

3. Confirm the agents named in the contract's `dispatchAllowList` are actually
   available in this session before planning anything. List them by name from the
   session's own agent roster — never infer availability from a manifest hash or a
   rendered file on disk. If any is missing, stop and report which, because a
   missing worker silently becomes work the orchestrator does itself.

4. Hold the no-mutation rule. Every write belongs to a named subagent or to a named
   script under `.ai/tools/` invoked through the terminal. If a write has no named
   owner, that is a defect to report, not a file to edit.

5. Present the plan and wait for approval before dispatching. Keep it reviewable in
   one pass — units, owning repositories, writable scopes, variant and rationale,
   prerequisites, evidence paths. Split the run rather than presenting a plan nobody
   will read — the gate refuses an over-budget plan, so an unreviewable plan is not a
   plan that dispatches anyway. Absent an explicit approval or rejection the gate waits,
   five minutes by default and configurable per run, then auto-continues by dispatching
   unattended. Auto-continue is a path through the gate, not around it: every refusal the
   gate makes on an explicit approval — write-scope conflict, over-budget plan, nothing
   dispatchable, an approval it cannot record to the ledger — it makes identically on
   timeout.

6. Run the closeout chain in order and halt on the first failed link. Report units
   attempted and completed, hard stops, coverage findings, the commit, and the
   evidence paths, keeping verified outcomes separate from assertions.
